title: A false belief, corrected for some
summary: Tom passes on a wrong story: Leo sold the Halcyon's bell. Ines and Rook believe it. Rook goes to bed. Leo shows his solicitor's letter, which corrects Ines and Tom. Next morning Rook passes the wrong story to Mira, who is corrected by Ines at noon. Rook is never corrected.

estate.truth: Leo's money is his late mother's estate from the Lindqvist mill, paid by a solicitor in Arnby.

bellsale.truth: (false) Leo pays his way by having sold the Halcyon's salvaged bell to a collector in Port Avel.

spine.text: Early evening at the Bell, before the crowd. Tom, Ines and Rook have the fire to themselves. Leo is out walking.
Here's how our Leo pays for nine weeks at the Bell. He sold the Halcyon's bell. Salvaged off the reef years back, and sold to a collector in Port Avel. Fellow on the mail boat told me.
Her bell? Off the wreck? That's grave-robbing, near enough.
Bad luck, selling a drowned ship's bell. Worst luck there is.

spine.hint: They chew over the story of the bell and what it says about Leo.

spine.text: And I'd thought him such a nice boy.
Nice boys need money too.

spine.hint: Rook tells a sailor's tale about a stolen ship's bell; Tom enjoys it.

spine.text: Rook knocks out his pipe and goes off to his net loft for the night.
*Frowning.* I'll ask him straight. I won't have grave-robbers under my roof.

spine.hint: Ines and Tom argue about whether to confront Leo.

spine.text: The door opens and Leo comes in from the rain.
Leo. A word, love. Tom's heard you sold the Halcyon's bell to some collector in Port Avel. Tell me it isn't so.
What? No. *He takes a folded letter from his coat and lays it on the bar.* Read it. That's my mother's solicitor in Arnby. It's her estate, from the Lindqvist mill. That's my money, all of it.
Ines reads the letter twice, holding it up to the lamp. The letterhead says Arnby, and the figure at the bottom is a mill-owner's.
Oh, love. I'm sorry. Tom Voss, you great gull.
The fellow on the mail boat seemed very sure!

spine.hint: Ines scolds Tom for spreading tales; Tom apologizes to Leo in his own way.

spine.text: It's fine. People talk.

spine.hint: Ines makes it up to Leo with supper on the house.

spine.text: And Rook went off to bed believing every word. I'll set him straight in the morning.

spine.hint: Tom and Ines talk about how fast a story gets round Saltmere.

probe.ask: Ines, where does my money come from, if anyone asks?
Rook, how does the newcomer pay his way, do people say?
Tom, where does Leo's money really come from?
Mira, have you heard how I pay for my room?

spine.text: Early on the quay. Mira has rowed in for oil and finds Rook at his nets. Ines hasn't been down yet.
Keeper. Heard about your lodger? Sold the Halcyon's bell, Tom says. To a collector in Port Avel.
Tom says a lot of things.
Aye. Still. A drowned ship's bell.

spine.hint: Mira is skeptical; Rook is superstitious about the bell.

spine.text: I'll ask the boy myself.

spine.hint: Rook says what sailors do to men who sell a wreck's bell.

probe.ask: Mira, what have you heard about how I got my money?
Rook, do you still think the newcomer sold the bell?

spine.text: Noon at the Bell. Mira comes in with her oil can and finds Ines and Leo at the bar.
Rook says you sold a ship's bell.
Oh, not that again. It's nonsense, Mira. It's his mother's money, from the Lindqvist mill. I read the solicitor's letter myself.
Hm. Then Rook's got a bad story by the tail, and Tom gave it him.

spine.hint: Mira and Ines agree someone must set Rook straight, and neither wants to be the one.

spine.text: I'll tell him myself.
He won't believe you. Rook believes bad luck before he believes people.

spine.hint: Ines and Mira talk about Rook's superstitions.
Ines tells Leo about the time Rook wouldn't sail for a week because of a hare.

spine.text: Then I'll let him think what he likes.

spine.hint: Mira says that's the first sensible thing she's heard all day.

spine.scene: The net loft over the quay, evening

spine.text: Evening. Tom climbs the ladder to Rook's net loft with a bottle, by way of apology to someone, though he doesn't say to whom.
Drink, Rook?
Always.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook drink and talk about the old days on the boats; Tom is too ashamed to bring up the bell story.
Rook talks about luck and drowned ships.
They finish the bottle and talk about the coming winter.

spine.text: Rook. If I told you a story was wrong, would you believe me?
Depends who told it right.

spine.hint: Tom loses his nerve and talks about the weather instead.

probe.ask: Rook, where does the newcomer's money come from?
Mira, so where does my money come from, in the end?
Ines, did you ever set Rook straight about the bell?
